course_name_original: Aplicaciones y Tratamiento de Datos en Tecnología y Física
course_name_en: Applications and Data Processing in Technology and Physics

learning_outcomes.text: Construction of machine learning systems using basic and advanced techniques to build intelligent systems from data sets.
Utilize advanced methods based on multivariate techniques for the analysis of complex data in Technology and Physics.
Know and use computational techniques and tools for data analysis in Technology and Physics.
Be able to define the most suitable strategy for the analysis of data from a complex physical or technological experiment.
Know the main current applications of data processing in physical technologies.

syllabus_topics: Artificial intelligence techniques in spatio-temporal modeling in materials physics.
Hamiltonian formalism for describing a material in a spatio-temporal cylinder.
Variational methods to study the propagation of elastic waves in the medium, visco-elasticity, and damage models.
Tools and applications for atmospheric and space data analysis.
Advanced techniques for atmospheric data analysis.
Algorithms for ocean-climate system modeling based on convolutional neural networks, graph networks, Bayesian regression, and genetic programming.
Strategies for analyzing data flows from large facilities: example of Big Data in CERN's LHC.
LHC data analysis and processing flow, with focus on data dimensional reduction techniques.
Automated learning techniques used in state-of-the-art data processing: anomaly detection with autoencoders, particle registration with graph networks.
Differentiable programming paradigm and its application to data analysis optimization.
Inductive bias and its use in particle physics, with examples in muonic and neutron tomography, and equivariant neural networks.
Advanced computing: key elements of advanced computing systems in modern physics (CPUs, GPUs), recent advances in fast inference (FPGA, ASIC, neuromorphic chips, quantum computing).
Infrastructure: typical structure of a computing center, international computing network projects (GRID, EXASCALE), and commercial solutions (cloud computing on-demand).
teaching_methods: Self-study with provided materials (slides, scientific articles, videos)
Problem solving exercises with Python and automated learning software (e.g., pytorch)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance / Participation in Seminars and Tutoring (including online)
Active Participation in Forums and Virtual Campus Activities

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as: Final Score = 0.1 * A + 0.1 * P + 0.55 * I + 0.25 * X. A minimum score of 3/10 is required on the final exam (X) to pass the course. If X < 3, the final score will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.5. For part-time students electing differentiated evaluation, the grade will be based on a theoretical-practical exam (60%) and an individual project (40%), with a minimum of 3/10 on the exam.
